# 2 Baruch Chapter 12 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 12:3 — "my wrath" vs. "my anger"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "my-wrath" | Literal — the Syriac rugza/hemtha |
| LOGOS | "my wrath" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "my anger" | "Anger" is more natural; less archaic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Wrath" (not "anger") is the standard theological term for divine judicial anger in apocalyptic — it carries eschatological weight that "anger" lacks in English.

---

## 12:4 — "had leave from me" vs. "had my permission"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "until-he-had-leave-from-me" | Literal idiom for formal permission |
| LOGOS | "until he had leave from me" | Formal English idiom |
| PNEUMA | "He had my permission" | More natural; "permission" for "leave" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Had leave from me" is the established English idiom for divinely granted permission (cf. KJV, RSV tradition). "Permission" is modern and correct but loses the formal grant register.

---

## 12:5 — "before I have resolved to chastise it"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "before-I-have-resolved-to-chastise [it]" | Literal with bracketed implied object |
| LOGOS | "before I have resolved to chastise it" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "unless I have decided to discipline it first" | "Decided" for "resolved"; "discipline" for "chastise" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Resolved to chastise" preserves both the deliberative sense (divine decision) and the punitive sense (chastisement as correction). PNEUMA's "decided to discipline" is accurate but loses the gravity of the language.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
